conventions.convention: Four filtration-like families are kept distinct: raw natural F^0_t = sigma(B_s : 0 <= s <= t); raw right limit F^0_{t+} = intersection over u > t of F^0_u; completed raw Fbar^0_t = sigma(F^0_t union N), where N is the family of subsets of P-null members of F^0_infty; and usual augmentation F_t = intersection over u > t of Fbar^0_u. Then F^0_t is contained in Fbar^0_t, which is contained in F_t; every F_t contains N; (F_t) is right-continuous; the strong Markov theorem is stated only for (F_t), while the deterministic Markov theorems are stated for both (F^0_t) and (F_t).

A stopping time is a map tau : Omega -> [0, infinity] with {tau <= t} in F_t for every t >= 0; the stopped sigma-algebra is F_tau = {A in F : A intersect {tau <= t} in F_t for every t >= 0}; the strict test {tau < t} in F_t is interchangeable with the non-strict one only when the filtration is right-continuous; and for deterministic tau = t_0 one has F_tau = intersection over t >= t_0 of F_t, which is F_{t_0} under right-continuity.

Quadratic variation is defined only along a named deterministic partition sequence with mesh tending to 0, and every partial sum is taken in two declared conventions (step convention, and partial-increment convention that adds the squared terminal increment and coincides with the step value at partition points); no partition-independent object is defined, and the convergence mode (pointwise, uniform, or uniform in probability) is part of each later statement.

Ito integration is carried out under the standing hypothesis (H) of def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand (B adapted to (F_t), increments B_t - B_s independent of F_s with law N(0, t - s)); elementary predictable integrands are left-endpoint steps H_s = sum_k xi_k 1_{(t_k, t_{k+1}]}(s) with bounded F_{t_k}-measurable xi_k; integrands are identified as (dt tensor P)-classes; and localization uses the canonical times tau_n = inf{t : int_0^t H^2 >= n} wedge n.

Process identities on the Ito page are equalities up to indistinguishability (or equalities of L^2(P)-classes at a fixed deterministic time); exceptional null sets are carried explicitly in conventions such as B_tau := 0 on {tau = infinity}, and the localized integral is the unique continuous version.

The Brownian zero set is read through the all-path continuous, jointly measurable version B-hat indistinguishable from B; Z = {t >= 0 : B-hat_t = 0} is closed and nonempty for every outcome, Z_T is compact, lambda(Z_T) is measurable, and almost-sure statements about Z transfer to the zero set of B.

Unbounded operators carry their domains as part of their data; T is contained in S means containment of graphs; the adjoint T* is defined only for densely defined T by Riesz representability of x -> <Tx, y>; symmetric means T contained in T*, self-adjoint means T = T*, essentially self-adjoint means the closure is self-adjoint; and the resolvent sign convention is R_T(z) = (z - T)^{-1}, the parameter appearing with a plus sign in front of T.

Deficiency subspaces are K_+ = ker(T* - i) and K_- = ker(T* + i), with deficiency indices their Hilbert dimensions; the Cayley transform is C_T = (T - i)(T + i)^{-1}; and the unitary-group sign convention is U(t) = e^{itT} with generator G = iT, equivalently T = -iG and D(T) = D(G).

Imported bounded-PVM calculus used by the unbounded theory: E is a projection valued measure (orthogonal projections, E(B cap C) = E(B)E(C), strong countable additivity); E_x(B) = <E(B)x, x> and E_{x,y}(B) = <E(B)x, y> with |E_{x,y}|(X) <= ||x|| ||y||; the bounded integral satisfies ||Phi_E(f)x||^2 = int |f|^2 dE_x; and the unbounded integral f(E) has domain {x : int |f|^2 dE_x < infinity}.

load_bearing.statement: Four families are distinguished: raw natural F^0_t = sigma(B_s : 0 <= s <= t), raw right limit F^0_{t+} = intersection_{u>t} F^0_u, completed raw Fbar^0_t = sigma(F^0_t union N) with N the subsets of P-null events of F^0_infty, and usual augmentation F_t = intersection_{u>t} Fbar^0_u; then F^0_t subset Fbar^0_t subset F_t, every F_t contains N, (F_t) is right-continuous, and the strong Markov theorem is stated for (F_t) while the deterministic Markov theorems are stated for both (F^0_t) and (F_t).

For every s >= 0 and every bounded Borel functional Phi on R^{[0,infinity)}, E[Phi((B_{s+t})_{t>=0}) | F_s] = Psi_Phi(B_s) almost surely with Psi_Phi(x) = int Phi(x + w) mu(dw), and the same identity holds with F^0_s in place of F_s; the increment process (B_{s+t} - B_s)_{t>=0} is independent of F_s with the finite-dimensional marginals of Wiener measure.

For a stopping time tau of the usual augmentation with tau < infinity almost surely: B_tau is F_tau-measurable, the increment process (B_{tau+t} - B_tau)_{t>=0} is independent of F_tau with the finite-dimensional marginals of Wiener measure, and E[Phi((B_{tau+t})_{t>=0}) | F_tau] = Psi_Phi(B_tau) almost surely for every bounded Borel functional Phi.

A partition sequence of [0, T] is a sequence of partitions with mesh tending to 0; today two partial sums are attached (step convention, and partial-increment convention adding the squared terminal increment) whose difference is at most the squared maximal oscillation; the quadratic variation is the limit along the named sequence in the mode each statement declares, and no partition-independent object is defined.

For a real continuous Brownian Ito process X_t = X_0 + int_0^t b_s ds + int_0^t sigma_s dB_s and f in C^{1,2}([0, infinity) x R), up to indistinguishability f(t, X_t) = f(0, X_0) + int_0^t (d_t f + b d_x f + (1/2) sigma^2 d_xx f)(s, X_s) ds + int_0^t sigma_s d_x f(s, X_s) dB_s, with the stochastic integral the localized Ito integral of the predictable locally square-integrable process sigma d_x f(., X).

X is a real continuous Brownian Ito process when X_0 is finite and F_0-measurable, b is progressively measurable with int_0^t |b_s| ds < infinity almost surely, sigma is predictable with int_0^t sigma_s^2 ds < infinity almost surely, and X_t = X_0 + int_0^t b_s ds + int_0^t sigma_s dB_s up to indistinguishability (the multidimensional version sums over the m driving Brownian coordinates).

For a continuous Brownian Ito process X driven by an m-dimensional Brownian motion, [X^i, X^j]_t = int_0^t (sigma sigma^T)^{ij}_s ds up to indistinguishability, the covariation existing on every finite horizon for every deterministic vanishing-mesh partition sequence and both partial-sum conventions uniformly in probability; and every pathwise absolutely continuous part has zero covariation with every continuous process.

For a predictable H with E int_0^T H^2 ds < infinity, the Ito integral int_0^T H dB is the L^2(P) limit of the elementary integrals I_T(H^n) for bounded elementary H^n converging to H in L^2(dt tensor P); the limit is shown independent of the approximating sequence by the following lemma, and int_0^t H dB is defined by applying the construction to H 1_{[0,t]}.

A self-adjoint operator T on a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a unique regular projection valued measure E on the Borel sigma-algebra of R with D(T) = {x : int lambda^2 dE_x(lambda) < infinity} and Tx = int lambda dE(lambda)x on D(T); conversely a regular PVM E on R yields a self-adjoint operator int lambda dE with that domain, and E is its spectral PVM.

The map T -> U(t) = e^{itT}, computed by the Borel functional calculus, is a bijection from the set of self-adjoint operators on H onto the set of strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups; its inverse assigns to U its generator G and the self-adjoint operator T = -iG, with D(T) = D(G) exactly the set of vectors where t -> U(t)x is differentiable at 0 and (1/t)(U(t)x - x) -> iTx there.

With usual augmented Brownian filtration: every Z in L^2(F_T) has Z = EZ + int_0^T H dB for a predictable finite-energy H unique modulo (dt tensor P)-null sets, and E[Z | F_t] = EZ + int_0^t H dB up to indistinguishability; every cadlag local martingale M satisfies M_t = M_0 + int_0^t H dB for a predictable locally square-integrable H, such H is unique, and M has a continuous version.

concerns.concern: Wrong source title on 15 items of the Ito-integral pair. The Step-5a audit entry refuter:8:8 (confirmed nonfatal, repaired only in the routed carrier) found that the PDF at https://diamhomes.ewi.tudelft.nl/~avandervaart/books/stochint.pdf has the title page 'Martingales, Diffusions and Financial Mathematics', yet the source titles read 'Aad van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, ...' in lem-cross-ito-isometry, def-progressively-measurable-and-predictable-process, lem-adapted-continuous-processes-are-progressively-measurable, lem-elementary-ito-integral-is-independent-of-the-step-representation, thm-density-of-elementary-predictable-processes-in-predictable-l2, thm-ito-integral-process-has-a-continuous-martingale-version, def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes, lem-general-ito-integral-is-independent-of-the-approximating-sequence-and-ae-representative, thm-stopping-an-ito-integral, def-locally-square-integrable-predictable-brownian-integrand, thm-localized-ito-integral, thm-quadratic-variation-of-an-ito-integral, ex-covariance-of-two-deterministic-ito-integrals, cex-pathwise-riemann-stieltjes-integration-does-not-construct-the-brownian-ito-integral and cex-product-measure-ae-equality-is-not-pointwise-equality-of-integrands. The numbered results cited (Definition 5.20, Lemma 5.22, Theorem 5.26, etc.) are then attributed to the wrong book; the URL points to the correct document.

Fact [A4] states 'If a unitary V satisfies ||Vu|| = ||u|| and V(K_+) = K_-, then U := C_T direct-sum (-V) is unitary on H' and cites thm-partial-isometry-characterizations. The cited item characterizes partial isometries by U*U being the orthogonal projection onto (ker U)^perp (and UU* the projection onto ran U); it says nothing about direct sums or about unitarity of a direct sum, so the citation supports less than the fact asserted (the missing argument is elementary but is not in the cited statement).

Fact [A2] asserts 'two Hilbert spaces are unitarily isomorphic exactly when their orthonormal bases have the same cardinality' and cites thm-existence-of-a-maximal-orthonormal-family together with thm-hilbert-space-with-a-given-orthonormal-basis-is-ell-two-of-the-index-set. The cited items state existence/completeness of a maximal orthonormal family and the isometric isomorphism H -> ell^2(I) for a given basis respectively; the unitary-isomorphism criterion for equal cardinalities has to be assembled from the two, and is not stated in either cited item.

seams_checked.note: Checked the declared cross-group prerequisite in both directions. Citing side: 20 declared dependency edges (9 distinct body-cited items) from the unbounded page, namely def-projection-valued-measure, lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm, thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral, thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism, thm-spectral-theorem-for-bounded-normal-operators-pvm-form, thm-support-and-uniqueness-of-the-spectral-measure, thm-multiplication-operator-form-of-the-bounded-normal-spectral-theorem, thm-cyclic-spectral-representation and thm-partial-isometry-characterizations, plus the implicitly used lem-neumann-series and the orthonormal-family interface. I opened each cited item and compared its current Statement/Definition with the citing text. The Facts [A2]-[A5] of thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators (bounded normal spectral PVM, support = sigma, unitarity and sigma(C) contained in S^1), the identities in lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed (||h(E)x||^2 = int |h|^2 dE_x, <h(E)x,y> = int h dE_{x,y}, h(E)* = conj h (E), multiplicativity, linearity, scalar dominated convergence), the PVM axioms used in def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm and ex-unbounded-multiplication-operator-and-its-domain (orthogonal projections, multiplicativity on intersections, strong countable additivity), and the multiplication/cyclic models used in thm-canonical-spectral-type-decomposition all match the cited statements without changing domain, quantifier, hypothesis, direction or conclusion. Two composite citations that assert more than the cited statement literally says are recorded as concerns against the citing items (thm-von-neumann-self-adjoint-extension-parameterization [A4]; cor-self-adjoint-extension-exists-iff-deficiency-indices-agree [A2]); no defect was found in any group-c item itself.
